chapter: Jack Laine and the New Orleans scene
title: Laine's trumpeters, Vega, and Willie Guitar
summary: Laine rotated trumpeters; Loyacano ranks Vega above Armstrong and recalls bassist Willie Guitar.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: first group that played in the Reliance band? That's Aviga on trumpet, was he? Well, you see,

I don't ever remember of Jack only having one band. Uh, he had, well, like I said before, he had the cream of the crop and he could switch them around. And he was fair about the whole thing. He had several trumpet players and well enough to make four or five bands. And instead of giving one man all the work, he'd switch. He had a fellow named Pete D. Tran. Played terrific trumpet, too. Uh, wasn't there a valve trombonist that played with... Oh, Bill Gallaty. Yeah, he was the champ. I never heard anybody play like him. Was he the daddy of this Gallaty boy that played? Bill Gallaty playing trumpet, yeah. Yeah. They. You see this, Pete D. Tran's, I never seen a man yet play a trumpet on the side of his mouth. That's the way he played it. That's the way he learned to play it. That's the way he got his ambassure. And he couldn't play in the center. But Vega, oh, Louis Armstrong at his best, uh, Buddy Bull, or any of them. None of them topped Vega in my category. That's, uh... No, sir. Not only I, but many, many other old-time musicians will swear that Vega was the greatest. He had it all over these other fellas, uh, because of the fact that he read music, the first start off. And you talk about hitting Cs, Ds, and E's above the staff. He did that when I was a kid. Oh, yes. He used to play tunes like the Wild Cherry Rag and the Black and White Rag. It was real difficult to play. I mean, it was, it was difficult even for a string. And yet he used to run those things to death. Uh, what about this
fantastic story about this fella by the name of Willie Guitar who played the bass and lived on music?
That's true. Is that true? Yeah, that's true. He played in Jack's band too? Yeah, sometime he wore a red
flannel under shirt too. That's true. In the summertime. Well now, uh, what's, uh, the outfit that you remember, uh, that you played with in your audience before you left here?
